data.mechanism: When methionine is scarce, PKM2 interacts with the GATOR2 complex and keeps it from relaying the 'nutrients present' signal, so mTORC1 stays off. The authors propose that stabilising the PKM2-GATOR2 interaction would mimic methionine starvation. Same double-negative logic as Sestrin2 for leucine and CASTOR1 for arginine.
data.mechanism_beginner: Without methionine, PKM2 holds GATOR2 back, so mTORC1 stays off.
data.context: The methionine route via PKM2 converges on GATOR2, the same complex read by Sestrin2 (leucine) and CASTOR1 (arginine); the SAM route via SAMTOR acts one step further on, at GATOR1-KICSTOR.
data.boundary: One study in cultured human cells (SANG2026). Whether PKM2 binds GATOR2 directly or through another protein, and on which subunit, is not stated in the abstract, so the step is marked unresolved. Cell and chemoproteomic data do not show that this sensor matters for mTORC1 in a whole organism. Not yet replicated.
